scope: Proposition 7.4 (Conditional fields at a cluster stop) of the manuscript “The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents” (preprints/The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-October-6-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 233 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cec129cca8c2a0a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 70. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a seed stop in an initial free parent of label b0, or the composite wired stop defined above. Let A, S, W0, E be its limiting explored set, seed trace, initial wall, and retained stopped sigma-field. The set A is connected to the original boundary, and every component O of D \ A is simply connected. Conditionally on E , h|O = mO + hO , mO − b0(O) ∈ 2aZ, (7.10) where the hO are independent zero-boundary GFFs. Here b0(O) is the label of its initial parent chamber; it is 0 in the initial free domain and ±a in a wired hole. The labels are tight on every finite family of pointed components. On every compact subset of D away from W0 ∪S, A has zero area and the full conditional mean M is the locally integrable piecewise constant function mO. On the same region, Equation (7.6) gives the full zero-extended conditional GFF law of h − M, also for tests whose supports meet A. Locally M is the limit of the finite signed odd-hole contributions of the discovered clusters, with the initial parent label added. These statements hold for every member of a specified countable family of sweeps and observable indexed stops, each conditional only on its own retained state. For a composite wired stop, every O is contained in one pointed limiting wired hole. The conclusions use the global exploration of the original h; they do not require a separate lattice sweep selected from that limiting hole.
